text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] severity=page cluster=cluster-prod-3 node=gpu-node-12 alert=GPU_ECC_SPIKE threshold=5m link=<https://monitoring.company/alerts/1853008765|view>

maria (oncall): paging — I'm on it. seeing repeated NVRM Xid logs from gpu-node-12, looks like a driver/GPU fault.

maria (oncall): quick checks: `kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-node-12` -> Ready/NotReady flapping. pods on node include model-serving replicas for `redwood/gpt-prod`.

dave: ping — I can take infra if needed. any customer-facing errors yet?

alyssa: metrics show elevated 502s from the inference gateway starting ~1853008600. ~1.2k failed requests in last 10m, concentrated in eu-west region. customers affected: a handful of enterprise tenants (IDs queued to notify).

maria (oncall): grabbing logs from the node now. `ssh ops@gpu-node-12 'dmesg | tail -n 80 | grep -i NVRM'`

maria (oncall): pasted output:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:0b:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:0b:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12346.000123] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:0b:00): 13, GPU page fault on channel 0000
```

irene: Xid=79 & 13 — typical driver reset + ECC/page-fault mix. are we also seeing container OOMs or just driver resets?

maria (oncall): containers are restarting — kubelet reports `EvictionThreshold met` and some pods crashlooping. not typical OOM, looks correlated with GPU resets. logs from `model-serving` show `cuMemAlloc failed` and `invalid device pointer` errors.

samuel: prioritize node isolation. plan: cordon -> drain (evict gpu workloads) -> restart driver on node -> if resets continue, reboot node and open vendor ticket. I'll draft commands.

samuel: commands:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
ssh ops@gpu-node-12 'sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver'  # or reload modules
# if restart fails: reboot node
```

maria (oncall): doing cordon+drain now — starting evictions. will watch rollout of replicas to other nodes.

incident-bot: autoscaler: k8s-cluster autoscaler triggered; scaled up nodepool-gpu by +2 instances to absorb evicted pods.

dave: good. once pods land on other nodes, confirm that inference latency returns to normal. alyssa, can you confirm which customers saw degraded SLA?

alyssa: sending that list to CS and legal. immediate impact: 3 enterprise customers saw >5% failed calls; standard-tier users saw intermittent latency increase but <1% errors. I'll prepare notification draft.

maria (oncall): restarted driver on gpu-node-12 — `systemctl status nvidia-driver` now shows active, but dmesg still shows sporadic Xid 79 events (1-2/min). not fully clean.

irene: if Xid events freq > 3/min we should consider full node reboot or cordon permanently and reprovision. also collect NVML logs: `/var/log/nvidia/*` + `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,DRIVER,DIAGNOSTIC` and attach to ticket.

maria (oncall): grabbing NVML output:
```
# nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,DRIVER,DIAGNOSTIC
Attached GPUs : 1
Product Name : A100-SXM
Driver Version : 525.85.12
Board ID : GPU-abcdef12
ECC Errors Recorded: Corrected: 14 Uncorrected: 0
```

samuel: corrected ECC errors are non-zero, that's likely root cause. open ticket with vendor (NVIDIA) and include board ID + dmesg + nvml logs. I'll start the ticket and paste link here.

samuel: vendor ticket created: <https://vendor-support/CASE-98765|CASE-98765>

alyssa: customer-notice draft: "We observed a partial service disruption affecting inference requests in eu-west due to GPU instability on a subset of nodes. We mitigated by draining affected nodes and shifting traffic; full remediation is in progress." Sending to legal for approval.

maria (oncall): update: after driver restart + draining, traffic errors dropped to baseline for most customers. we're still seeing occasional Xid 79 spikes on the hardware. I'm going to cordon gpu-node-12 permanently for now.

dave: agreement — cordon will avoid re-scheduling until hardware replaced. also set routing policy: prefer nodes in other AZs for critical customers until post-mortem.

maria (oncall): executed `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12` and added node to replacement queue.

irene: followups: collect nvml logs from any node with ECC>0, correlate to job ids/timestamps. add a check in runtime: if corrected ECC > 10 in 1h, alert to oncall.

samuel: add to runbook: when Xid==79 or corrected ECC spikes -> cordon node, drain, collect nvml + dmesg, restart driver, if persists reboot and open vendor ticket. I'll update the runbook PR.

alyssa: customer notifications sent to affected customers (IDs included). CS will follow up with remediation timeline. No escalations yet.

maria (oncall): handing off to dave for overnight monitoring. notes for handoff:
- node gpu-node-12 cordoned and set for replacement
- vendor ticket CASE-98765 created, NVML/dmesg attached
- watch for Xid events >5 in 10m: escalate to eng-sre and file hotfix if driver regression suspected
- if new nodes show ECC corrected counts increasing, consider pausing auto-scheduler for GPU nodepool

dave: ACK. will monitor logs and keep SOC/CS updated. I'll check `/var/log/nvidia/` every hour and run `nvidia-smi -q -d DIAGNOSTIC` on any suspect node.

incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated; page closed. next action: postmortem required (owner=maria). link: <https://incidents.company/1853008765|incident record>

maria (oncall): thanks everyone. creating the postmortem draft now with timeline, impacted customers, remediation steps, and action items (replace hardware, add ECC alert, update runbook).

alyssa: nice work coordinating. :thumbsup:

dave: will follow up if anything flares. good handoff.

maria (oncall): leaving final note: number summary — ~1.2k failed calls, 3 enterprise customers with >5% errors, node taken OOS. Post-mortem will include verification steps for the fix.

irene: add test to staging: simulate driver-reset and ensure autoscaler+fallback work within SLA.

maria (oncall): copy. closing thread once postmortem published.
